## Assessment Summary

The top keeper from sniper_stage2_grinder fails the OP-16 primary gate with edge_capture=373.48 (<771 floor). While it excels at avoiding losses on J loser days (turning them into profits), it severely underperforms on J winner days, capturing only a fraction of the available edge. This indicates likely overfit to non-J days and insufficient capture of the core J-edge signal.

### (1) Genuine edge or overfit?
Overfit. The edge_capture of 373.48 is below the 50% OP-16 floor (771), triggering automatic rejection. Performance on J winner days is poor: 4/29 captured 53% of available edge ($181.84 vs $342), 5/01 captured 0% ($0 vs $470), 5/04 captured 26% ($191.64 vs $730). Conversely, J loser days were converted to profits (5/05: +$202.41 vs -$260 J loss; 5/06: $0 vs -$300; 5/07: +$470.8 vs -$165 combined J losses). However, OP-16 edge_capture only rewards capturing winner-day edge and penalizing loser-day losses—not profiting on loser days. The strong loser-day performance does not compensate for weak winner-day capture under this metric, suggesting the grinder optimized for non-J day profitability at the expense of the core edge.

### (2) Knob changes driving improvement vs baseline
Unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest. The input provides the final parameter combo but no baseline comparison from the sniper_overnight_grinder output. Without knowing the starting parameters, we cannot isolate which specific knob changes (vol_mult, body_min_cents, strike_offset, etc.) drove the observed performance. A Stage-1 backtest comparing this combo to the baseline is necessary for attribution.
